about: FICTIONAL medical inventory for the demo (38 items). Quantities and locations are invented; label expiry dates are not defined. Historical evidence is kept separate from current stock. CC0.

expiry_rules.rule: The label date does not prove stability under all flight conditions.
expiry_rules.app: Show the label date plus a space-uncertainty notice; never move the date automatically.

expiry_rules.rule: Du et al. tested 35 formulations; at 28 months 9 flight and 17 ground samples met the USP content criterion.
expiry_rules.app: Show an educational alert; do NOT extrapolate percentages to an individual drug.

expiry_rules.rule: 2023 re-analysis: degradation in space relatively small compared with controls; repackaging can matter a lot.
expiry_rules.app: Do not claim that every drug expires earlier in space.

expiry_rules.rule: Individual stability under mission conditions unknown.
expiry_rules.app: State: NO SPACE DATA; label date is administrative only, not a guarantee of efficacy.
Show EXPIRED (LABEL); do not recommend administration.
Show DEPLETED; exclude from available resources.

expiry_rules.rule: Specific evidence of a stability failure exists.
expiry_rules.app: Show STABILITY ALERT with the reference; do NOT compute a new date without batch, formulation, packaging and storage data.
Show months until the label date and an uncertainty warning; do not infer an effective expiry date.

expiry_rules.rule: There is no universal shelf-life reduction applicable to the 38 items.

expiry_rules.app: The label date alone does not guarantee stability throughout a space mission. Check the available data and the protocol.

stability_references.label: Du et al. 2011, AAPS J: 35 formulations flown on the ISS
Wotring 2016: 9 medications after long ISS storage
